The following information was taken from Kay Company’s accounting records for the year ended December 31, 2014:
Increase in raw materials inventory | $15,000
Decrease in finished goods inventory | 35,000
Raw materials purchased | 430,000
Direct manufacturing labor payroll | 200,000
Factory overhead | 300,000
Freight-out | 45,000
There was no work in process inventory at the beginning or end of the year. Kay’s 2014 cost of goods sold is
questions.explanation: Raw materials used = $430,000 purchased - $15,000 added to inventory = $415,000. With no work in process at either end, cost of goods manufactured = $415,000 + $200,000 + $300,000 = $915,000. Finished goods fell $35,000, meaning that much came out of stock and was sold, so COGS = $915,000 + $35,000 = $950,000. Freight-out is a selling expense and never enters COGS.
questions.explanationJa: 使用した原材料 = 購入 $430,000 − 在庫増加 $15,000 = $415,000。期首・期末とも仕掛品がないので、当期製品製造原価 = $415,000 + $200,000 + $300,000 = $915,000。製品在庫が $35,000 減少したということは、その分が在庫から出て販売されたことを意味するので、売上原価 = $915,000 + $35,000 = $950,000。発送運賃（freight-out）は販売費であり、売上原価には入らない。

questions.stem: During the month of March 2014, Nale Co. used $300,000 of direct material. At March 31, 2014, Nale’s direct material inventory was $50,000 more than it was at March 1, 2014. Direct material purchases during the month of March 2014 amounted to
questions.explanation: Purchases = materials used + increase in inventory = $300,000 + $50,000 = $350,000. The extra $50,000 was bought but not consumed, so it is sitting in inventory at month end.
questions.explanationJa: 購入額 = 使用額 + 在庫の増加 = $300,000 + $50,000 = $350,000。増えた $50,000 は購入したが消費されなかった分であり、月末に在庫として残っている。

questions.stem:
Fab Co. manufactures textiles. Among Fab’s 2014 manufacturing costs were the following salaries and wages:
Loom operators | $120,000
Factory foreman | 45,000
Machine mechanics | 40,000
What was the amount of Feb’s 2014 direct manufacturing labor?
questions.explanation: Only the loom operators work directly on the product, so direct labour is $120,000. The foreman supervises and the mechanics maintain the machines; both are necessary to production but cannot be traced to specific units, so they are indirect labour and form part of factory overhead.
questions.explanationJa: 製品に直接作業しているのは織機のオペレーターだけなので、直接労務費は $120,000 である。職長は監督業務、整備工は機械の保守を担当しており、いずれも生産に不可欠だが個々の製品に跡付けられないため、間接労務費として製造間接費を構成する。

questions.stem:
The fixed portion of the semivariable cost of electricity for a manufacturing plant is a
Period cost | Product cost
questions.explanation: Electricity for a manufacturing plant is a cost of production, so all of it, fixed portion included, is absorbed into the product and becomes an expense only when the product is sold. A period cost would be expensed as incurred, which is how selling and administrative costs behave.
questions.explanationJa: 工場の電力費は製造にかかる費用なので、固定部分も含めてすべて製品原価に吸収され、その製品が販売されて初めて費用となる。期間原価であれば発生時に費用処理されるが、それは販売費・一般管理費の扱いである。

questions.stem:
Gram Co. develops computer programs to meet customers’ special requirements. How should Gram categorize payments to employees who develop these programs?
Direct costs | Value-added costs
questions.explanation: The programmers' pay can be traced to the specific customer program they write, so it is a direct cost. It is also value-added, because writing the program is precisely what the customer is paying for; storage, waiting, and inspection would be the non-value-added activities.
questions.explanationJa: プログラマーの給与は、担当する特定の顧客向けプログラムに跡付けられるので直接費である。同時に付加価値を生む費用でもある。プログラムを書くことこそ顧客が対価を支払っている対象だからである。保管・待機・検査といった活動が非付加価値活動にあたる。

questions.stem: In a job-costing system, issuing indirect materials to production increases which account?
questions.explanation: Indirect materials cannot be traced to a job, so they are debited to manufacturing overhead control along with all other actual indirect costs, and reach the jobs later through the application rate. Direct materials would go to work in process control instead.
questions.explanationJa: 間接材料は個々の指図書に跡付けられないので、他の実際発生間接費とともに製造間接費統制勘定に借記され、後から配賦率を通じて各指図書へ流れていく。直接材料であれば仕掛品統制勘定に振り替えられる。

questions.stem:
Costs are accumulated by responsibility center for control purposes when using
Job order costing | Process costing
questions.explanation: Responsibility accounting is independent of the product-costing method. Whichever system is used to attach costs to output, costs are also collected by the manager who controls them so that performance can be evaluated.
questions.explanationJa: 責任会計は製品原価計算の方法とは独立している。産出物に原価を割り当てるためにどの方式を用いるかにかかわらず、業績を評価できるよう、原価はそれを管理する責任者ごとにも集計される。

questions.stem:
Birk Co. uses a job order cost system. The following debits (credit) appeared in Birk’s work in process account for the month of April 2014:
April | Description | Amount
1 | Balance | $ 4,000
30 | Direct materials | 24,000
30 | Direct manufacturing labor | 16,000
30 | Factory overhead | 12,800
30 | To finished goods | (48,000)
Birk applies overhead to production at a predetermined rate of 80% of direct manufacturing labor costs.
Job No.5, the only job still in process on April 30, 2014, has been charged with direct manufacturing labor of $2,000. What was the amount of direct materials charged to Job No.5?
questions.explanation: The ending work in process balance is $4,000 + $24,000 + $16,000 + $12,800 - $48,000 = $8,800, all of which belongs to Job No. 5. Its labour is $2,000 and its applied overhead is 80% of that, $1,600, so direct materials = $8,800 - $2,000 - $1,600 = $5,200.

questions.stem:
In a job cost system, manufacturing overhead is
An indirect cost of | A necessary element in
jobs | production
questions.explanation: Overhead is indispensable to production, since nothing could be made without the factory, its power, and its supervision. It is nonetheless indirect, because none of those costs can be traced to an individual job and must instead be applied through a rate.
questions.explanationJa: 製造間接費は生産に不可欠である。工場も電力も監督もなければ何も作れないからである。それでも間接費であることに変わりはない。これらの費用は個々の指図書に跡付けられず、配賦率を通じて割り当てるほかないからである。

questions.stem:
Under Pick Co.’s job order costing system manufacturing overhead is applied to work in process using a predetermined annual overhead rate. During January 2014, Pick’s transactions included the following:
Direct materials issued to production | $90,000
Indirect materials issued to production | 80,000
Manufacturing overhead incurred | 125,000
Manufacturing overhead applied | 113,000
Direct labor costs | 107,000
Pick had neither beginning nor ending work in process inventory. What was the cost of jobs completed in January 2014?
questions.explanation: Work in process is charged with direct materials, direct labour, and overhead applied, never overhead incurred: $90,000 + $107,000 + $113,000 = $310,000. With no work in process at either end, all of it was completed. The $80,000 of indirect materials is already inside the overhead figures, and the $12,000 underapplied balance is disposed of separately.
questions.explanationJa: 仕掛品に賦課されるのは、直接材料費・直接労務費・配賦された製造間接費であって、実際発生額ではない: $90,000 + $107,000 + $113,000 = $310,000。期首・期末とも仕掛品がないので、その全額が完成している。間接材料費 $80,000 は既に製造間接費の数値に含まれており、配賦不足 $12,000 は別途処理される。

questions.stem: A direct manufacturing labor overtime premium should be charged to a specific job when the overtime is caused by the

choices.label: B
choices.text: Customer’s requirement for early completion of job.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Management’s failure to include the job in the production schedule.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Management’s requirement that the job be completed before the annual factory vacation closure.

questions.explanation: An overtime premium is charged to a specific job only when that job caused it. A customer who demands early delivery is the cause, so the premium is part of that job's cost. Overtime arising from a heavy overall schedule, poor scheduling, or a plant shutdown is caused by the operation as a whole and belongs in overhead, to be spread over all jobs.
questions.explanationJa: 残業割増賃金を特定の指図書に賦課するのは、その指図書が原因となった場合だけである。顧客が早期の納品を要求したのであれば、それが原因なので割増分はその指図書の原価となる。全体の受注量の多さ、日程計画の不備、工場の一斉休業といった事情による残業は、操業全体に起因するものなので、製造間接費に含めて全指図書へ配分する。

questions.stem: A company services office equipment. Some customers bring their equipment to the company’s service shop; other customers prefer to have the company’s service personnel come to their offices to repair their equipment. The most appropriate costing method for the company is
questions.explanation: Each repair is different: a distinct machine, a distinct fault, and a distinct amount of labour and parts, whether done in the shop or at the customer's office. Costs must therefore be accumulated per job. Process costing suits identical units flowing continuously, which is the opposite situation.
questions.explanationJa: 修理は一件ごとに異なる。対象の機械も不具合も、要する作業量も部品も違い、それは工場で行うか顧客先で行うかを問わない。したがって原価は案件ごとに集計しなければならない。総合原価計算は同一の製品が連続的に流れる場合に適した方法であり、これとは逆の状況を想定している。

questions.stem:
In developing a predetermined variable factory overhead application rate for use in a process costing system, which of the following could be used in the numerator and denominator?
Numerator | Denominator

choices.label: A
choices.text: Actual variable factory overhead | Actual machine hours

choices.label: B
choices.text: Actual variable factory overhead | Estimated machine hours

choices.label: C
choices.text: Estimated variable factory overhead | Actual machine hours

choices.label: D
choices.text: Estimated variable factory overhead | Estimated machine hours

questions.explanation: A predetermined rate must be available before the period begins, so both terms are estimates: estimated overhead over estimated activity. Any use of actual figures would defeat the purpose, since actual amounts are not known until the period is over.
questions.explanationJa: 予定配賦率は期間が始まる前に用意されていなければならないので、分子・分母とも見積値を用いる。すなわち見積製造間接費を見積操業度で割る。実際額を使えば目的が損なわれる。実際額は期間が終わるまで分からないからである。

questions.stem:
A job order cost system uses a predetermined fixed factory overhead rate based on normal activity and expected fixed cost. At the end of the year, underapplied fixed overhead might be explained by which of the following situations?
Actual volume | Actual fixed costs

choices.label: A
choices.text: Greater than normal | Greater than expected

choices.label: B
choices.text: Greater than normal | Less than expected

choices.label: C
choices.text: Less than normal | Greater than expected

choices.label: D
choices.text: Less than normal | Less than expected

questions.explanation: Fixed overhead is underapplied when applied is less than incurred. Applied falls short when actual volume is below the normal activity used to set the rate, and incurred rises when actual fixed costs exceed the budget. Both conditions therefore have to point the same way.
questions.explanationJa: 固定製造間接費が配賦不足になるのは、配賦額が発生額を下回るときである。配賦額が足りなくなるのは、実際操業度が配賦率設定に用いた基準操業度を下回るときであり、発生額が膨らむのは実際固定費が予算を超えるときである。したがって2つの条件は同じ方向を指していなければならない。

questions.stem:
Worley Company has underapplied variable overhead of $45,000 for the year ended December 31, 2014.
Before disposition of the underapplied overhead, selected December 31, 2014 balances from Worley’s accounting records are as follows:
Sales | $1,200,000
Cost of goods sold | 720,000
Inventories:
Direct materials | 36,000
Work in process | 54,000
Finished goods | 90,000
Under Worley’s cost accounting system, over or underapplied variable overhead is allocated to appropriate inventories and cost of goods sold based on year-end balances. There are no amounts of under or overapplied fixed overhead. In its 2014 income statements, Worley should report cost of goods sold of
questions.explanation: The underapplied amount is spread over the accounts that actually carry overhead: work in process $54,000, finished goods $90,000, and cost of goods sold $720,000, a total of $864,000. Direct materials are excluded because no overhead has been applied to them yet. COGS takes $720,000 / $864,000 x $45,000 = $37,500, giving $720,000 + $37,500 = $757,500.
questions.explanationJa: 配賦不足額は、実際に製造間接費を含んでいる勘定に配分する。すなわち仕掛品 $54,000、製品 $90,000、売上原価 $720,000 の合計 $864,000 である。直接材料はまだ製造間接費が配賦されていないので除外する。売上原価への配分額は $720,000 ÷ $864,000 × $45,000 = $37,500 なので、$720,000 + $37,500 = $757,500 となる。

questions.stem:
Parat College allocates support department costs to its individual schools using the step method.
Information for May 2014 is as follows:
Support departments | Support departments
Maintenance | Power
Costs incurred | $99,000 | $54,000
Service percentages provided to:
Maintenance | -- | 10%
Power | 20% | --
School of Education | 30% | 20%
School of Technology | 50% | 70%
100% | 100%

questions.explanation: FIFO equivalent units for materials = (100 x 50% to finish) + (400 - 100 started and completed) + (200 x 75%) = 50 + 300 + 150 = 500. Cost per equivalent unit uses only the current-period cost: $720,000 / 500 = $1,440. Ending inventory carries 150 equivalent units, so 150 x $1,440 = $216,000. questions.stem:
The Forming Department is the first of a two-stage production process. Spoilage is identified when the units have completed the Forming process. Costs of spoiled units are assigned in the period spoilage is identified. The following information concerns Forming’s conversion costs in May 2014:
Units | Conversion cost
Beginning work in process(50% complete) | 2,000 | $10,000
Units started during May | 8,000 | 75,500
Spoilage――normal | 500
Units completed and transferred | 7,000
Ending work in process (80% complete) | 2,500
Using the weighted-average method, what was Forming’s conversion cost transferred to the second production department?
questions.explanation: Spoilage is detected at the end of the process, so spoiled units are 100% complete for conversion and must be counted. Equivalent units = 7,000 completed + 500 spoiled + (2,500 x 80%) = 9,500. Cost per unit = ($10,000 + $75,500) / 9,500 = $9.00. The transferred amount absorbs the normal spoilage: (7,000 + 500) x $9.00 = $67,500. Omitting the spoiled units gives $63,000.
questions.explanationJa: 仕損は工程の終点で発見されるので、仕損品は加工費について100%完成しており、換算量に数えなければならない。完成品換算量 = 完成品7,000 + 仕損500 + (2,500 × 80%) = 9,500。単位当たり原価 = ($10,000 + $75,500) ÷ 9,500 = $9.00。次工程への振替額は正常仕損を吸収する: (7,000 + 500) × $9.00 = $67,500。仕損品を数えないと $63,000 になる。

questions.stem: In computing the current period’s manufacturing cost per equivalent unit, the FIFO method of process costing considers current period costs

choices.label: B
choices.text: Plus cost of beginning work in process inventory.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Less cost of beginning work in process inventory.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Plus cost of ending work in process inventory.

questions.explanation: FIFO keeps the two layers apart: the beginning inventory is finished and transferred out at its own cost, and the current period's costs are divided only by the work actually done this period. That is what makes the FIFO unit cost a clean measure of current performance, whereas the weighted-average rate blends in last period's cost.
questions.explanationJa: 先入先出法は2つの層を分けて扱う。期首仕掛品は自らの原価を抱えたまま完成・振替され、当期発生原価は当期に実際に行われた作業だけで割る。これにより先入先出法の単位原価は当期の業績を素直に表す指標となる。これに対し平均法の単価は前期の原価を混ぜ込んでしまう。

questions.stem:
A process costing system was used for a department that began operations in January 2014.
Approximately the same number of physical units, at the same degree of completion, were in work in process at the end of both January and February. Monthly conversion costs are allocated between ending work in process and units completed. Compared to the FIFO method, would the weighted-average method use the same or a greater number of equivalent units to calculate the monthly allocations?
Equivalent units for weighted-average compared FIFO
January | February
questions.explanation: The two methods differ only in how they treat beginning inventory. January is the department's first month, so there is no beginning inventory and the two give identical equivalent units. February opens with the January ending inventory, and weighted-average counts the work already done on it while FIFO excludes it, so weighted-average is greater.

choices.label: B

questions.explanationJa: 期末仕掛品は66⅔%完成しており、検査は40%の時点で行われるので、これらの単位は既に検査点を通過している。したがって正常仕損費を分担しなければならない。期末仕掛品の数量が完成振替量と等しいので、両者が均等に負担することになり、期末仕掛品の負担は50%となる。

questions.stem: In its April 2012 production, Hern Corp., which does not use a standard cost system, incurred total production costs of $900,000, of which Hern attributed $60,000 to normal spoilage and $30,000 to abnormal spoilage. Hern should account for this spoilage as

choices.label: C
choices.text: Period cost of $60,000 and inventoriable cost of $30,000.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Inventoriable cost of $60,000 and period cost of $30,000.

questions.explanation: Normal spoilage is an unavoidable cost of producing good units, so it stays in inventory and reaches the income statement only through cost of goods sold: $60,000 inventoriable. Abnormal spoilage should not have happened and provides no future benefit, so the $30,000 is written off as a period cost when incurred.
questions.explanationJa: 正常仕損は良品を生産するうえで避けられない原価なので、在庫に留まり、売上原価を通じて初めて損益計算書に現れる: $60,000 が棚卸資産原価となる。異常仕損は本来生じるべきでないもので将来の便益をもたらさないため、$30,000 は発生時に期間原価として費用処理する。

questions.explanation: Activity-based costing looks for the driver that actually causes the activity to be performed. Material handling is done component by component, so a unit with more components consumes more handling. questions.explanationJa: 活動基準原価計算では、その活動が実際に行われる原因となる要因（ドライバー）を探す。材料の運搬・取扱いは部品ごとに発生するので、部品点数の多い製品ほど多くの運搬活動を消費する。生産バッチ数は段取費のドライバーであり、他の2つは運搬とは無関係な単位レベルの指標である。

questions.stem:
What is the normal effect on the numbers of cost pools and allocation bases when an activity-based cost (ABC) system replaces a traditional cost system?
Cost pools | Allocation bases
questions.explanation: The whole point of ABC is to stop forcing dissimilar costs through one plant-wide rate. Costs are separated into many pools, one per activity, and each pool is assigned using the driver that causes it, so both the number of pools and the number of bases rise.
questions.explanationJa: ABCの本旨は、性質の異なる原価を一つの全社的な配賦率に押し込めるのをやめることにある。原価は活動ごとに多数のプールへ分けられ、各プールはそれを引き起こすドライバーによって配賦されるので、プールの数も配賦基準の数もともに増える。

questions.stem: Which of the following is true about activity-based costing?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It should not be used with process or job costing.

choices.label: B
choices.text: It can be used only with process costing.

choices.label: C
choices.text: It can be used only with job costing.

choices.label: D
choices.text: It can be used with either process or job costing.

questions.explanation: ABC is a way of assigning overhead, not a way of accumulating product cost, so it sits on top of whichever system the production process calls for. A job shop and a continuous process can both replace a single plant-wide rate with activity pools.
questions.explanationJa: ABCは製造間接費を割り当てる方法であって、製品原価を集計する方法ではないので、生産形態に応じて選ばれるどちらの制度の上にも乗せられる。個別受注生産でも連続生産でも、単一の全社的配賦率を活動別のプールに置き換えることができる。

questions.stem: In an activity-based costing system, what should be used to assign a department’s manufacturing overhead costs to products produced in varying lot sizes?

choices.label: C
choices.text: Relative net sales values of the products.

choices.label: D
choices.text: A product’s ability to bear cost allocations.

questions.explanation: Different overhead costs are driven by different things: setups by the number of production runs, inspection by the number of inspections, handling by the number of components. When lot sizes vary, a single base misstates cost systematically, charging large lots too much and small lots too little, so multiple driver relationships are needed.
questions.explanationJa: 製造間接費は費目ごとに異なる要因で発生する。段取費は生産バッチ数、検査費は検査回数、運搬費は部品点数によって動く。ロットサイズがばらつく場合、単一の配賦基準では原価が体系的に歪み、大ロットに過大に、小ロットに過小に賦課されてしまうので、複数の因果関係を用いる必要がある。

questions.stem:
In an activity-based costing system, cost reduction is accomplished by identifying and eliminating
All cost drivers | Non-value adding activities
questions.explanation: Cost drivers are not the problem; they are the measurement tool that reveals what causes cost, and eliminating them would leave the firm blind. What ABC targets is the non-value-adding activities themselves, such as moving, storing, and waiting, which consume resources the customer will not pay for.
questions.explanationJa: コストドライバーは問題ではない。原価が何によって生じるかを明らかにする測定の道具であり、これをなくせば企業は原価の姿を見失う。ABCが標的とするのは非付加価値活動そのもの、すなわち移動・保管・待機といった、顧客が対価を払わない資源消費である。

questions.stem:
Nile Co.’s cost allocation and product costing procedures follow activity-based costing principles.
Activities have been identified and classified as being either value-adding or non-value-adding as to each product. Which of the following activities, used in Nile’s production process, is nonvalue-adding?
questions.explanation: Storing raw materials changes nothing about the product; the material is identical before and after, and the customer would not pay more for having had it sit in a warehouse. Design, heat treatment, and drilling each transform the product in a way the customer values.
questions.explanationJa: 原材料の保管は製品を何ら変えない。材料は保管の前後で同一であり、倉庫に置かれていたからといって顧客が多く支払うことはない。設計・熱処理・穴あけは、いずれも顧客が価値を認める形で製品を変化させる活動である。

questions.stem:
Lane Co. produces main products Kul and Wu. The process also yields by-product Zef. Net realizable value of by-product Zef is subtracted from joint production cost of Kul and Wu. The following information pertains to production in July 2014 at a joint cost of $54,000:
Product | Units produced | Market value | Additional cost
after split-off
Kul | 1,000 | $40,000 | $ 0
Wu | 1,500 | 35,000 | 0
Zef | 500 | 7,000 | 3,000
If Lane uses the net realizable value method for allocating joint cost, how much of the joint cost should be allocated to product Kul?
questions.explanation: First remove the by-product: Zef's net realizable value = $7,000 - $3,000 = $4,000, leaving $54,000 - $4,000 = $50,000 of joint cost to allocate. Kul and Wu have no separable costs, so their net realizable values are the market values themselves: $40,000 and $35,000, totalling $75,000. Kul takes $50,000 x $40,000 / $75,000 = $26,667. Units produced are irrelevant under this method.
questions.explanationJa: まず副産物を取り除く: Zefの正味実現可能価額 = $7,000 − $3,000 = $4,000 なので、配賦すべき結合原価は $54,000 − $4,000 = $50,000 となる。KulとWuには分離後の追加原価がないので、正味実現可能価額は市場価値そのものであり、$40,000 と $35,000、合計 $75,000。Kulの配賦額 = $50,000 × $40,000 ÷ $75,000 = $26,667。この方法では生産数量は関係しない。

questions.stem: For purposes of allocating joint costs to joint products, the sales price at point of sales, reduced by cost to complete after split-off, is assumed to be equal to the

choices.label: D
choices.text: Sales price less a normal profit margin at point of sale.

questions.explanation: Working backwards from the final selling price and deducting the costs still to be incurred after split-off gives what the product was worth at the split-off point. That figure, the net realizable value at split-off, is the allocation base, and it lets products with different amounts of further processing be compared on the same footing.
questions.explanationJa: 最終販売価格から出発し、分離点以降に発生する原価を差し引くと、その製品が分離点において持っていた価値が求まる。この金額、すなわち分離点における正味実現可能価額が配賦基準となり、追加加工の程度が異なる製品同士を同じ土俵で比較できるようになる。

questions.stem:
Mig Co., which began operations in 2014, produces gasoline and a gasoline by-product. The following information is available pertaining to 2014 sales and production:
Total production costs to split-off point | $120,000
Gasoline sales | 270,000
By-product sales | 30,000
Gasoline inventory, 12/31/14 | 15,000
Additional by-product costs:
Marketing | 10,000
Production | 15,000
Mig accounts for the by-product at the time of production.
What are Mig’s 2014 cost of sales for gasoline and the by-products?
Gasoline | By-product
questions.explanation: Recognizing the by-product at production means its net realizable value is credited against the joint cost. By-product NRV = $30,000 - $10,000 - $15,000 = $5,000, so gasoline's cost becomes $120,000 - $5,000 = $115,000. Deducting the $15,000 still in inventory leaves cost of sales of $100,000. The by-product shows no cost of sales at all, because its cost was already removed from the joint pool.
questions.explanationJa: 副産物を生産時点で認識するということは、その正味実現可能価額を結合原価から控除することを意味する。副産物のNRV = $30,000 − $10,000 − $15,000 = $5,000 なので、ガソリンの原価は $120,000 − $5,000 = $115,000 となる。期末在庫 $15,000 を差し引いた売上原価は $100,000。副産物の売上原価はゼロである。その原価は既に結合原価プールから取り除かれているからである。

questions.stem:
The following information pertains to a by-product called Moy:
Sales in 2012 | 5,000 units
Selling price per unit | $6
Selling costs per unit | 2
Processing costs | 0
Inventory of Moy was recorded at net realizable value when produced in 2013. No units of Moy were produced in 2014. What amount should be recognized as profit on Moy’s 2014 sales?
questions.explanation: Recording the by-product at net realizable value when it is produced recognizes the entire margin at that moment. The later sale merely converts inventory into cash at the carrying amount, so no further profit arises: $6 - $2 = $4 was already taken in the year of production. Note that the source material's date labels are inconsistent, but the answer turns only on the timing of recognition.
questions.explanationJa: 副産物を生産時点で正味実現可能価額により計上することは、その時点で利益の全額を認識することを意味する。その後の販売は在庫を帳簿価額のまま現金に換えるだけなので、追加の利益は生じない。$6 − $2 = $4 は既に生産年度に取り込まれている。なお教材側の年号表記に食い違いがあるが、この設問の答えを決めるのは認識のタイミングだけである。

questions.stem: Kode Co. manufactures a major product that gives rise to a by-product called May. May’s only separable cost is a $1 selling cost when a unit is sold for $4. Kode accounts for May’s sales by deducting the $3 net amount from the cost of goods sold of the major product. There are no inventories. If Kode were to change its method of accounting for May from a by-product to a joint product, what would be the effect on Kode’s overall gross margin?

choices.label: B
choices.text: Gross margin increases by $1 for each unit of May sold.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Gross margin increases by $3 for each unit of May sold.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Gross margin increases by $4 for each unit of May sold.

questions.explanation: As a by-product, May contributes $3 by reducing cost of goods sold. As a joint product, its $4 of revenue enters sales while the $1 selling cost drops below the gross margin line as a selling expense, and the joint cost merely moves between products without changing the total. Gross margin therefore improves by $1 per unit.
questions.explanationJa: 副産物として扱う場合、Mayは売上原価を減らす形で $3 を貢献する。連産品として扱えば、$4 の収益が売上高に計上され、$1 の販売費は売上総利益の下の行に落ちる。結合原価は製品間で移動するだけで総額は変わらない。したがって売上総利益は1単位当たり $1 だけ改善する。

questions.stem:
In accounting for by-products, the value of the by-product may be recognized at the time of
Production | Sale
questions.explanation: Both timings are acceptable. Recognizing at production credits the by-product's net realizable value against the joint cost and carries it as inventory; recognizing at sale leaves the joint cost with the main product and reports the by-product proceeds as other income or as a reduction of cost of goods sold when the sale occurs.
questions.explanationJa: どちらのタイミングも認められる。生産時点で認識する方法は、副産物の正味実現可能価額を結合原価から控除し、これを在庫として計上する。販売時点で認識する方法は、結合原価を主産物に残したまま、販売が生じた時点で副産物の収入を雑収益または売上原価の控除として報告する。

questions.stem:
Day Mail Order Co. applied the high-low method of cost estimation to customer order data for the first four months of 2014. What is the estimated variable order filling cost component per order?
Month | Order | Cost
January | 1,200 | $3,120
February | 1,300 | 3,185
March | 1,800 | 4,320
April | 1,700 | 3,895
6,000 | $14,520
questions.explanation: The high-low method uses only the extreme activity levels: March at 1,800 orders and $4,320, January at 1,200 orders and $3,120. Variable cost = ($4,320 - $3,120) / (1,800 - 1,200) = $1,200 / 600 = $2.00 per order. Choice B, $2.42, is the average total cost per order, which mixes in the fixed component.
questions.explanationJa: 高低点法は操業度の両極だけを使う。3月は1,800件で $4,320、1月は1,200件で $3,120。変動費 = ($4,320 − $3,120) ÷ (1,800 − 1,200) = $1,200 ÷ 600 = 1件当たり $2.00。選択肢Bの $2.42 は1件当たりの平均総原価であり、固定費部分が混ざっている。

questions.stem:
Sender, Inc. estimates parcel mailing costs using data shown on the chart below. The chart plots total cost in dollars against the number of parcels: the line meets the vertical axis at $15,000 when no parcels are mailed, and reaches $75,000 at 20,000 parcels. The chart plots total cost in dollars against the number of parcels: the line meets the vertical axis at $15,000 when no parcels are mailed, and reaches $75,000 at 20,000 parcels. The chart plots total cost in dollars against the number of parcels: the line meets the vertical axis at $15,000 when no parcels are mailed, and reaches $75,000 at 20,000 parcels. The chart plots total cost in dollars against the number of parcels: the line meets the vertical axis at $15,000 when no parcels are mailed, and reaches $75,000 at 20,000 parcels. The chart plots total cost in dollars against the number of parcels: the line meets the vertical axis at $15,000 when no parcels are mailed, and reaches $75,000 at 20,000 parcels.
What is Sender’s estimated cost for mailing 12,000 parcels?
questions.explanation: Read the fixed cost off the vertical intercept, $15,000, and the slope from the two known points: ($75,000 - $15,000) / 20,000 parcels = $3.00 per parcel. Cost for 12,000 parcels = $15,000 + (12,000 x $3.00) = $51,000. Choice A is the variable portion alone, and choice D applies the average cost at 20,000 parcels, which overstates the rate.
questions.explanationJa: 縦軸との交点から固定費 $15,000 を読み取り、既知の2点から傾きを求める: ($75,000 − $15,000) ÷ 20,000個 = 1個当たり $3.00。12,000個の原価 = $15,000 + (12,000 × $3.00) = $51,000。選択肢Aは変動費部分だけ、選択肢Dは20,000個時点の平均原価を単価として当てはめたもので、率を過大に見積もっている。

questions.stem: Which of the following may be used to estimate how inventory warehouse costs are affected by both the number of shipments and the weight of materials handled?
questions.explanation: Two independent variables, number of shipments and weight handled, act on one dependent variable, warehouse cost. Multiple regression is the technique that fits a separate coefficient to each. Simple correlation measures the strength of a single pairwise relationship and cannot separate the two effects.
questions.explanationJa: 出荷回数と取扱重量という2つの独立変数が、倉庫費用という1つの従属変数に作用している。それぞれに個別の係数を当てはめる手法が重回帰分析である。単純相関は1対1の関係の強さを測るだけで、2つの効果を分離できない。

questions.stem:
Sago Co. uses regression analysis to develop a model for predicting overhead costs. Two different cost drivers (machine hours and direct materials weight) are under consideration as the independent variable.
Relevant data were run on a computer using one of the standard regression programs, with the following results:
Machine hours | Coefficient
Y Intercept | 2,500
B | 5.0
R2 = .70
Direct materials weight | Coefficient
Y Intercept | 4,600
B | 2.6
R2 = .50
What regression equation should be used?
questions.explanation: R squared says how much of the variation in overhead each driver explains. Machine hours explain 70% against direct materials weight's 50%, so machine hours is the better independent variable and its own intercept and slope must be used together: Y = 2,500 + 5.0X. Choices B and D mix the coefficients of one model with the intercept of the other.
questions.explanationJa: 決定係数R²は、各ドライバーが製造間接費の変動をどれだけ説明できるかを示す。機械時間は70%を説明し、直接材料重量は50%にとどまるので、機械時間の方が優れた独立変数であり、その切片と傾きを組にして使わなければならない: Y = 2,500 + 5.0X。選択肢BとDは、一方のモデルの係数と他方の切片を混ぜてしまっている。

questions.stem:
In its first year of operations, Magna Manufactures had the following costs when it produced 100,000 and sold 80,000 units of its only product:
Manufacturing costs | Fixed $180,000
Variable | 160,000
Selling and admin. costs | Fixed | 90,000
Variable | 40,000
How much lower would Magna's net income be if it used variable costing instead of full absorption costing?
questions.explanation: The only difference between the two methods is the fixed manufacturing cost held in inventory. Fixed manufacturing cost per unit = $180,000 / 100,000 = $1.80, and 20,000 units remain unsold, so absorption costing defers 20,000 x $1.80 = $36,000 into inventory that variable costing expenses now. Fixed selling and administrative costs are period costs under both methods and never enter the comparison.
questions.explanationJa: 2つの方法の違いは、在庫に留まる固定製造原価だけである。単位当たり固定製造原価 = $180,000 ÷ 100,000 = $1.80。20,000単位が売れ残っているので、全部原価計算は 20,000 × $1.80 = $36,000 を在庫として繰り延べるが、直接原価計算はこれを当期の費用とする。固定販売費・一般管理費はどちらの方法でも期間原価であり、この比較には入らない。

questions.stem:
Using the variable costing method, which of the following costs are assigned to inventory?
Variable selling and | Variable factory
administrative costs | overhead costs
questions.explanation: Variable costing inventories only the variable manufacturing costs: direct materials, direct labour, and variable factory overhead. Selling and administrative costs are period costs whether they vary or not, because they are not incurred to make the product.
questions.explanationJa: 直接原価計算が棚卸資産に含めるのは変動製造原価だけであり、直接材料費・直接労務費・変動製造間接費がこれにあたる。販売費・一般管理費は変動費であっても期間原価である。製品を作るために発生した費用ではないからである。

questions.stem: At the end of Killo Co.'s first year of operations, 1,000 units of inventory remained on hand. Variable and fixed manufacturing costs per unit were $90 and $20, respectively. If Killo uses absorption coting rather than variable (direct) costing, the result would be a higher pretax income of
questions.explanation: Absorption costing attaches the $20 of fixed manufacturing cost per unit to inventory, so 1,000 unsold units carry 1,000 x $20 = $20,000 of cost into next period instead of expensing it now. The $90 variable cost is inventoried under both methods and makes no difference.
questions.explanationJa: 全部原価計算は単位当たり $20 の固定製造原価を在庫に付着させるので、売れ残った1,000単位が 1,000 × $20 = $20,000 の原価を当期の費用とせずに翌期へ繰り越す。変動費 $90 はどちらの方法でも棚卸資産に含まれるので、差を生まない。

questions.stem:
A manufacturing company prepares income statements using both absorption and variable costing methods. At the end of a period actual sales revenues, total gross profits, and total contribution margin approximated budgeted figures, whereas net income was substantially greater than the budgeted
amount. There were no beginning or ending inventories. The most likely explanation of the net income
increase is that, compared to budget, actual

choices.label: B
choices.text: Selling and administrative fixed expenses had decreased.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Sales prices and variable costs had increased proportionately.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Sales prices had declined proportionately less than variable costs.

questions.explanation: With no inventories the two methods report the same income, so the explanation must lie below the lines that came in on budget. Gross profit and contribution margin were both on target, which rules out anything affecting sales prices, variable costs, or manufacturing fixed costs. The only remaining item is fixed selling and administrative expense, and it must have come in lower than budget.
questions.explanationJa: 在庫がない以上、2つの方法の利益は一致するので、説明は予算どおりだった行より下に求めなければならない。売上総利益も貢献利益も予算どおりだったので、販売価格・変動費・固定製造原価に影響する事由はすべて排除される。残るのは固定販売費・一般管理費だけであり、これが予算を下回ったことになる。

questions.stem: A single-product company prepares income statements using both absorption and variable costing methods. Manufacturing overhead cost applied per unit produced in 2014 was the same as in 2013. The 2014 variable costing statement reported a profit whereas the 2014 absorption costing statement reported a loss. The difference in reported income could be explained by units produced in 2014 being

choices.label: B
choices.text: Less than the activity level used for allocating overhead to the product.

choices.label: C
choices.text: In excess of the activity level used for allocating overhead to the product.

choices.label: D
choices.text: In excess of units sold in 2014.

questions.explanation: When production is less than sales, the company sells out of inventory, and absorption costing releases the fixed manufacturing cost stored in those units into cost of goods sold on top of the current period's. Absorption income therefore falls below variable costing income, which can turn a variable costing profit into an absorption loss.
questions.explanationJa: 生産量が販売量を下回ると、企業は在庫を取り崩して販売することになり、全部原価計算では、それらの単位に蓄えられていた固定製造原価が当期分に上乗せされて売上原価へ流れ出す。したがって全部原価計算の利益は直接原価計算の利益を下回り、直接原価計算では黒字でも全部原価計算では赤字になりうる。
